metadata.title: The Red Violin Case — A2
metadata.synopsis: Joana precisa levar um violino emprestado ao salão de música e descobre duas formas de atravessar o rio.

scenes.title: A Delay at the Landing
scenes.narration: Joana reached the ferry landing with a red violin case. Inside was the violin she had borrowed from her teacher. She needed to return it at the music hall across the river. A notice said the ferry was delayed for repairs. The water was calm, but the large boat would not leave soon. She looked for another plan.
scenes.prompt: Why did Joana need to reach the music hall?

options.text: To collect a new violin case

scenes.explanation: The story says: "needed to return it at the music hall".

scenes.title: Other Ways across
scenes.narration: A landing worker pointed upstream. A riverside path led to a pedestrian bridge, then back along the other bank to the hall. Beside the landing, a licensed operator was preparing a smaller boat for a scheduled crossing. He had space for Joana and the closed case. She thanked the worker and checked both routes on the town map.

scenes.explanation: The story says: "led to a pedestrian bridge".

scenes.title: A Person to Help
scenes.narration: An older musician stood at the start of the riverside path. He was walking to the hall and offered to guide Joana. The boat operator called that his crossing was ready, too. Joana could walk with the musician or travel with the operator. Neither route changed her promise to return the violin safely. She held the case by its handle.
scenes.prompt: What did the older musician offer?

options.text: To guide Joana to the hall

scenes.explanation: The story says: "offered to guide Joana".

scenes.title: A Story on the Bridge
scenes.narration: Joana followed the musician along the path and over the bridge. He told her that her teacher had once played at the hall with him. At the north-bank entrance, they found the teacher waiting. Joana returned the closed red case and introduced her guide. The two musicians recognised each other. Her longer journey had brought more than a violin back to the hall.
scenes.prompt: How did the older musician know Joana's teacher?

options.text: They had played at the hall together
They had repaired the ferry together
They had borrowed Joana's violin together

scenes.explanation: The story says: "her teacher had once played at the hall with him".

scenes.title: A Seat by the Window
scenes.narration: Joana crossed in the operator's boat, keeping the closed case beside her seat. At the north landing, he showed her the short path to the music hall. Her teacher was waiting inside. After Joana returned the violin, he invited her to stay for the rehearsal. She chose a seat by the window and listened, relieved that the borrowed instrument was safely home.

authoringNotes.brief: Joana precisa levar um violino emprestado ao salão de música e descobre duas formas de atravessar o rio.

visualContinuity.characters: Joana, a 33-year-old woman with an oval face, brown eyes, straight black hair tied in a short ponytail, a navy coat, a cream scarf, dark trousers and low walking boots; she carries a hard red violin case. Joana's teacher is a 58-year-old man with short greying hair, a narrow face and a plain green cardigan. The older musician is a 72-year-old man with a white beard, a lined face and a brown wool coat. The boat operator is a 50-year-old woman with short black hair and a practical dark blue jacket.
visualContinuity.locations: A calm river town: ferry landing on the south bank, an upstream pedestrian bridge reached by a riverside path, and a music hall on the north bank. A licensed boat operator also works at the landing.
visualContinuity.clues: The borrowed violin stays closed inside its red case until the final hall. A notice at the ferry landing announces a repair delay. The upstream bridge and the boat operator are both introduced before the choice.
